newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares at new record despite summer lull.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares at new record despite summer lull.

text.p: A flurry of morning profit-taking and the absence of many players at the start of the summer holiday season failed to stop Danish share prices edging to a new record on Monday.

Mostly modest rises cancelled out even more modest falls, although BG Bank tumbled 10 crowns to 355.00, suffering from evaluations that is is overvalued after the breakdown of merger plans with mortgage lender Nykredit.
But the KFX top-20 index rose 0.07 point to 173.28 in overall bourse turnover of 1.16 billion crowns.
Its August future fell 0.35 point to 173.85, with 16 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
"The market will probably be relatively quiet tomorrow. We expect continued focus on Danisco and the banks but at the same time a thin mark. You can certainly feel that summer's here," a dealer said.
Danisco, expected to announce at least a 12.7 percent rise in profits when it publishes full-year results on Wednesday, closed six crowns up, at 433.00.
A total of eight of the top 20 shares rose, 11 fell and one was unchanged. --Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
